method.name: apply
method.description: Applies one frame this pipeline produced onto the row a peer holds. The receive half of the same crossing, here rather than in its own class because a frame's shape is decided by the send that made it, and a receiver reading it against a different plan is the failure both halves exist to prevent. [param held] is the row the receiver already has, as bytes, and may be empty for a peer holding nothing yet. Answers the values the receiver now holds, or an empty array when the frame does not read against [param schema]. A refusal never half-applies.

method.name: apply_window
method.description: Reads one windowed frame, answering every tick it repeats. A windowed frame carries a SEQUENCE rather than a state, so this answers a [code]samples[/code] array of [code]{tick, values}[/code] rather than one row. A caller that took only the newest would discard exactly the ticks the lane repeats the range to deliver.

method.name: confirm
method.description: Holds send [param index] of the last deferred pass until its datagram is stamped. Called AFTER the frame reached the carrier, because a pass answers what it wants to send and only the carrier knows what went out and in which datagram.

method.name: run
method.description: Runs one send pass over [param offers]. An offer is a [Dictionary] of [code]route[/code], [code]comp[/code], [code]channel[/code], [code]schema[/code], [code]values[/code], [code]recipients[/code] and [code]priority[/code]. The answer carries [code]sends[/code], one dictionary per recipient owed a row, plus the counts that say why a pass sent nothing: [code]caught_up[/code], [code]ungathered[/code] and [code]untrackable[/code].

method.name: set_encode_stage
method.description: Installs the stage every frame's bytes pass through. The shell routes every encode through a virtual a game may replace, so a native pipeline that encoded directly would drop that override on the floor and no game would learn it had happened until its wire changed shape. The callback receives [code](peer, tick, route, comp, mask, bytes)[/code] and answers the bytes that ride; an empty answer drops the frame, which is what the shell's stage already means. A callback that is set and cannot be called is a BROKEN stage rather than an absent one: the frame is dropped and counted rather than quietly encoded the native way, because falling back would hide the breakage behind traffic that looks correct.
